  "body": "# WalletTg code and storage (https://docs.ton.org/llms/contracts/standard/wallets/telegram/contract/content.md)



Every deployed wallet stores an immutable *trampoline* code. The trampoline code hash is `9149AE51C1E4689710CEBF7830297B16ACFBADB363A920A537893E7FFEECA768`. It is the root-cell hash of [`WalletTrampoline.boc`](https://github.com/ton-blockchain/tg-wallet-contract/blob/rev00/contracts/WalletTrampoline.boc).

## Trampoline [#trampoline]

The trampoline loads and executes the shared implementation from [configuration parameter `-123`](https://docs.ton.org/llms/foundations/config/content.md). The `-123 PUSHINT CONFIGOPTPARAM` instructions fetch the code cell, the trampoline turns it into a continuation and starts executing the code that processes incoming signed internal or external requests, and get-method calls.

```fift title="Excerpt from the WalletTrampoline.fif"
SETCP0
DUP IFNOT:<{        // method_id 0 = internal
  s1 PUSH           // copy body_slice
  SBITS             // n_bits of body_slice
  9 PUSHPOW2 LESS   // n_bits < 512, -1 or 0
  0 THROWIF         // n_bits < 512: exit 0
}>
-123 PUSHINT        // ... idx-in-config
CONFIGOPTPARAM      // ... cell | null, but we suppose it exists
CTOS BLESS          // ... continuation
DUP c3 POPCTR       // ... continuation
JMPX                // ... jump to WalletTg code to process
//                         an internal or external signed request
//                         or a getter call
```

## Active implementation [#active-implementation]

Validators can change the active shared implementation in [config param `-123`](https://actonscan.com/config?network=mainnet#config-parameter--123) by voting. Every mainnet WalletTg account uses this implementation — a wallet owner cannot pin a version, change the code, or opt out of code updates.

* Latest revision: [`rev00` tag in GitHub](https://github.com/ton-blockchain/tg-wallet-contract/tree/rev00).
* Revision code hash: `e30911420bef1191c09dce58b9df2b4ca4c2d9c383cc3b6a91170349ffa70e2c`.
* Source: [`WalletTg.tolk`](https://github.com/ton-blockchain/tg-wallet-contract/blob/rev00/contracts/WalletTg/WalletTg.tolk).

## Initial state [#initial-state]

TON derives the address from the hash of the original [`StateInit`](https://docs.ton.org/llms/foundations/messages/deploy/content.md), which contains the trampoline code and initial `Storage` data. The fields serialize in this order:

### Current storage [#current-storage]

| Field           |    Width | Initial value            | Current meaning                                      |
| --------------- | -------: | ------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------- |
| Revision prefix |   8 bits | `0x00` (`Rev00_Initial`) | Storage schema revision                              |
| `seqno`         |  32 bits | `0`                      | Expected sequence number for the next signed request |
| `subwalletId`   |  32 bits | Chosen by the client     | Wallet ID checked in each request header             |
| `publicKey`     | 256 bits | Anchor public key        | Current request-signing key                          |

The source defines mainnet default `subwalletId` `0x7FFF7F11` and testnet default `0x7FFF7FFD`. The selected ID is part of `StateInit` and must match each request header.

`publicKey` starts with the [anchor key](https://docs.ton.org/llms/contracts/standard/wallets/telegram/overview/content.md). Rotation replaces it with the new signing key.

Rotation changes only the storage, so the original `StateInit`, address, and trampoline code hash stay the same. Rebuilding `StateInit` with the new key would derive a different address.

## Getters [#getters]

| Getter               | Result    | Behavior                                                          |
| -------------------- | --------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `revision()`         | `uint8`   | Reads the stored revision prefix; does not call `Storage.load()`. |
| `seqno()`            | `uint32`  | Calls `Storage.load()` and returns `seqno`.                       |
| `get_subwallet_id()` | `uint32`  | Calls `Storage.load()` and returns `subwalletId`.                 |
| `get_public_key()`   | `uint256` | Calls `Storage.load()` and returns `publicKey`.                   |

After rotation, the `get_public_key()` getter returns the active signing key, not the anchor key.

## Storage and migration [#storage-and-migration]

`Storage.load()` runs `runMigrationAndUpdateC4()` when the stored prefix differs from `LAST_REVISION`. A transaction persists the migration when it commits [account data](https://docs.ton.org/llms/tvm/registers/content.md).

<Callout type="note">
  See [request failure behavior](https://docs.ton.org/llms/contracts/standard/wallets/telegram/messages/content.md) for external-send commit timing.
</Callout>

Revision 0 stores prefix `0x00`, has no old layouts in `UnionOfOldStorages`, and uses a no-op `runMigrationAndUpdateC4()`. Later revisions must preserve prior layouts and define migrations to the current schema. The [migration rules](https://github.com/ton-blockchain/tg-wallet-contract/blob/rev00/MIGRATION.md) also require existing messages and getters to remain compatible as new ones are added.

<Callout type="caution">
  The call to a `revision()` get-method can report an older storage revision while the account already executes newer shared code. It does not identify the active implementation.
</Callout>

  * [migration code](https://github.com/ton-blockchain/tg-wallet-contract/blob/rev00/contracts/WalletTg/migration.tolk)

  "body": "# WalletTg: Telegram wallet contract (https://docs.ton.org/llms/contracts/standard/wallets/telegram/overview/content.md)



WalletTg (`tg-wallet`, TgWallet, or Telegram Wallet) is the TON wallet contract used by [Telegram's native Gram wallet](https://docs.ton.org/llms/onboarding/wallet-apps/telegram/content.md).

## Features [#features]

* Receive Gram, jettons, and non-fungible tokens (NFTs) at a stable address.
* Send a [single message](https://docs.ton.org/llms/contracts/standard/wallets/telegram/messages/content.md) or a [batch of up to 255 messages](https://docs.ton.org/llms/contracts/standard/wallets/telegram/messages/content.md).
* Connect to decentralized applications (dApps) through [TON Connect](https://docs.ton.org/llms/applications/ton-connect/overview/content.md).
* Import [12-word phrases or 24-word rotation mnemonics](https://docs.ton.org/llms/contracts/standard/wallets/telegram/integrate/content.md) in compatible wallet apps.
* [Rotate the signing key](https://docs.ton.org/llms/contracts/standard/wallets/telegram/integrate/content.md) while keeping the same address.
* Submit signed internal requests through a [relayer](https://docs.ton.org/llms/contracts/standard/wallets/telegram/interact/content.md) that attaches Gram for processing.

## Shared implementation [#shared-implementation]

Each account stores immutable *trampoline* code. The trampoline loads the shared implementation from [configuration parameter `-123`](https://docs.ton.org/llms/foundations/config/content.md), while each account keeps its own balance and storage.

<Image src="/images/wallets/telegram/architecture.svg" darkSrc="/images/wallets/telegram/architecture.svg" alt="WalletTg accounts keep trampoline code and local storage while executing shared implementation code from configuration parameter minus 123." width="900" height="390" />

Validators approve configuration changes through voting. An update changes the implementation used by every WalletTg account on that network. Wallet owners cannot change the implementation or opt out of updates.

The brief [contract reference](https://docs.ton.org/llms/contracts/standard/wallets/telegram/contract/content.md) documents storage and upgrade migration behavior.

## Two-key rotation architecture [#two-key-rotation-architecture]

WalletTg is the only TON wallet contract that can rotate its public signing key without changing its address. Its [24-word rotation mnemonic](https://docs.ton.org/llms/contracts/standard/wallets/mnemonics/content.md) combines two 12-word [multichain mnemonics](https://docs.ton.org/llms/contracts/standard/wallets/mnemonics/content.md): the first half derives an *anchor key*, and the second half derives a *signing key*. The complete rotation mnemonic preserves both the anchor and the signing keys.

Initially, an anchor key is also the signing key. The contract's [`StateInit`](https://docs.ton.org/llms/foundations/messages/deploy/content.md) uses the anchor public key as its first signing public key. The *rotation* replaces the current on-chain signing key with a new one. It requires a request signed by the current private key and a rotation proof signed by the new private key. The anchor key does not change.

After rotation, only the new signing key authorizes requests — the anchor key continues to derive the original address, but it cannot restore signing access on its own.

<Callout type="caution">
  Composing a new `StateInit` with the new signing key would yield a different address. The original `StateInit` must always be composed with the original signing key, which is the anchor key.
</Callout>

## Comparison with V5 [#comparison-with-v5]

[Wallet V5](https://docs.ton.org/llms/contracts/standard/wallets/v5/content.md) is the default general-purpose wallet contract on TON. It does not rotate the signing key, has an optional extensions support, and does not allow code upgrades. Additionally, V5 uses a different [messages format](https://docs.ton.org/llms/contracts/standard/wallets/v5-api/content.md) compared to the [WalletTg messages](https://docs.ton.org/llms/contracts/standard/wallets/telegram/messages/content.md).

WalletTg is used primarily by Telegram. Wallet apps and services should default to Wallet V5 for all new TON wallet contracts, but also support importing rotation mnemonics and managing WalletTg contracts.

<Callout type="note">
  Compare wallet capabilities in the [table](https://docs.ton.org/llms/contracts/standard/wallets/comparison/content.md).
</Callout>

  "body": "# Telegram Money — the native Gram wallet (https://docs.ton.org/llms/onboarding/wallet-apps/telegram/content.md)



Telegram Money is a [mainnet](https://docs.ton.org/llms/start-here/content.md) wallet on The Open Network (TON) for receiving assets and connecting to decentralized apps (dApps) through [TON Connect](https://docs.ton.org/llms/applications/ton-connect/overview/content.md).

* **On-chain transfers:** send Gram to Telegram users, including those who have not opened the wallet yet. Transfers execute on TON through the [WalletTg smart contract](https://docs.ton.org/llms/contracts/standard/wallets/telegram/overview/content.md).

* **Sponsored fees:** Telegram covers network fees for a daily allowance of five free transfers through [gasless transactions](https://docs.ton.org/llms/contracts/standard/wallets/gasless/content.md).

* **One wallet across devices:** an [encrypted cloud backup](#disable-backup-or-update-the-phrase) allows using the same wallet across devices without manual imports. It splits the wallet key into **three** parts stored in data centers on **three** continents.

* **Connect dApps once:** TON Connect connections sync across devices without reconnecting each one. Each device needs the current wallet key, restored from the cloud backup or the recovery phrase.

* **Control the keys:** disable cloud backup or [rotate the signing key](#disable-backup-or-update-the-phrase) without changing the wallet address. The current recovery phrase also allows importing the wallet into another compatible wallet app.

* **Shared contract upgrades:** validators can vote to [upgrade the shared wallet implementation](https://docs.ton.org/llms/contracts/standard/wallets/telegram/overview/content.md) to add features and improvements for all Telegram Money users at once, without user action. These upgrades require more than 75% of the total validator weight — neither Telegram nor anyone else can bypass validator approval to perform them.

<Callout type="note">
  For *testnet* wallets, use [wallet.ton.org](https://docs.ton.org/llms/onboarding/wallet-apps/web/content.md) or [manage development wallets](https://ton-blockchain.github.io/acton/docs/wallets) with the [Acton toolchain](https://docs.ton.org/llms/contracts/acton/content.md).
</Callout>

## Open or restore a wallet [#open-or-restore-a-wallet]

In Telegram Desktop, open the main menu and select <kbd>Money</kbd>. This entry appears only when Telegram enables wallet access for the account.

* To restore access on a device, use the recovery phrase:

  1. Open the Money menu and select <kbd>Keys & Backup</kbd>.
  2. Select <kbd>Restore from recovery phrase</kbd> when Telegram offers phrase-based restoration, then enter the current phrase.

* To display the phrase in Telegram Desktop, open Money's menu, select <kbd>Keys & Backup</kbd>, then <kbd>Show Recovery Phrase</kbd>.

  <Callout type="danger">
    The recovery phrase gives control of the wallet and funds. Store it securely — never share the recovery phase in plain text.
  </Callout>

* To import the phrase in another app, use an app that supports the [WalletTg](https://docs.ton.org/llms/contracts/standard/wallets/telegram/overview/content.md) contract and its [rotation mnemonic format](https://docs.ton.org/llms/contracts/standard/wallets/mnemonics/content.md).

## Confirm the address and connect a dApp [#confirm-the-address-and-connect-a-dapp]

1. Copy the wallet address from Telegram Money and check it in a [mainnet explorer](https://docs.ton.org/llms/onboarding/explorers/content.md).
2. Start a [TON Connect](https://docs.ton.org/llms/applications/ton-connect/overview/content.md) session from the dApp and confirm its name in Telegram Money.
3. Review each transaction or signing request before approving it. A connection alone does not authorize a transaction.

## Disable backup or update the phrase [#disable-backup-or-update-the-phrase]

An encrypted backup splits the wallet key into 3 parts stored across 3 continents, and then reassembles it on devices. It is done off-chain, so this backup is unavailable for wallets imported from the recovery phrase.

To disable the backup, select <kbd>Keys & Backup</kbd>, then <kbd>Disable Backup</kbd>. This reveals the phrase and asks for confirmation of selected words. When key rotation is available, <kbd>Update Secret Phrase</kbd> is optional and unchecked by default.

* Without the phrase update, Telegram disables backup after the current phrase passes the word check. The signing key does not change, so existing copies remain current.
* With the phrase update, Telegram shows the rotation fee. It prepares and displays a new phrase, then checks selected words. It disables backup only after the key rotation succeeds. Words 1-12 keep the address anchor, and words 13-24 become the new signing key.

<Callout type="note">
  If rotation fails or is canceled, the current key and backup remain unchanged.
</Callout>

If rotation succeeds but the following backup-disable request fails, the new phrase becomes the current while the backup may remain enabled with the old phrase. Keep the new phrase and verify the backup state until the request succeeds.

## Create TON Connect links [#create-ton-connect-links]

To direct users from a dApp to Telegram Money, prepare a payload for its [TON Connect link formats](https://docs.ton.org/llms/onboarding/wallet-apps/deep-links/content.md):

1. Build the [standard connection query](https://docs.ton.org/llms/applications/ton-connect/core-concepts/content.md) using `v`, `id`, `r`, and optional `trace_id`. For Telegram Money, use a lowercase `id`, include `ton_addr` in the [connection request](https://docs.ton.org/llms/applications/ton-connect/api-reference/protocol/content.md), and use an HTTPS `manifestUrl` without credentials or a fragment.
2. Start with the percent-encoded query without its leading `?`. Encode any remaining literal `-`, `.`, `_`, and `~` as `%2D`, `%2E`, `%5F`, and `%7E`, respectively. Preserve existing percent-encoded bytes.
3. Replace `&` with `-`, `=` with `__`, and `%` with `--`.
4. Use the result as `<PACKED>` in the link format. The templates already include the `tonconnect-` prefix.

To reopen a pending request, omit `r` and include `v=2`, the existing connection's lowercase `id`, and the UUID `trace_id` sent with that request. Apply the same packing steps. The request data must already have been sent through the connection.

To decode a payload, restore `--` to `%`, then `__` to `=`, then `-` to `&`, before parsing the query.

## Learn more [#learn-more]

* [WalletTg contract](https://docs.ton.org/llms/contracts/standard/wallets/telegram/overview/content.md)

## Gram and fees [#gram-and-fees]

*Gram* (GRAM) is the TON's primary [cryptocurrency](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cryptocurrency). It is used to pay for the execution of smart contracts, the storage of their data, and network traffic. Such payments are called [fees](https://docs.ton.org/llms/foundations/fees/content.md).

## Mainnet and testnet [#mainnet-and-testnet]

There are two instances of TON blockchain: mainnet and testnet.

*Mainnet* is the "real" network. It's where actual payments in Gram are made. Applications use the mainnet by default.

The other network is *testnet*, and it is used by TON developers to check that their applications work correctly before deploying them to mainnet. It uses "test coins" that barely have any value.

Usually, when the TON blockchain gets an update, it is first deployed to testnet, and then to mainnet after a brief period of testing, so sometimes they may run different software. Also, their [configuration](https://docs.ton.org/llms/foundations/config/content.md), availability, and throughput might be different.
